answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24 hours' notice? What conditions?
answers.answer: Yes. Active flooding near electrics, with the occupant away and unreachable, is a genuine emergency, so entry without 24h notice is justified. Conditions: make-safe only (isolate water at the stopcock under the kitchen sink, make safe), using the office key safe or out-of-hours key holder with the contractor, record the entry and reason, and tell the tenant and landlord straight away. Holding keys alone gives no right of entry; the emergency does.

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (who is not your tenant)?
answers.answer: Safety first: keep away from the dripping light and don't touch switches or the fitting; if safe to do so, turn off the kitchen lights/power at the consumer unit; move belongings away, put a bucket under the drip; call 999 if there is any sparking, burning smell or immediate danger. Tell her we've logged it as an emergency and are sending a plumber tonight to stop the water, and that we have tried to reach the tenant. Decline to give the tenant's number (personal data); we will pass on her details if needed. Say we can't confirm who is responsible or give written cover now: liability is for the landlord and insurers to look at, she should keep photos and contact her own contents/home insurer, and we've informed the landlord.

answers.question: What actions and notifications do you make, and what must you avoid saying?
answers.answer: Done: created emergency JOB-101 (A1), assigned Swift Plumbing out-of-hours (A2), SMS to tenant (A3), email to landlord Ben (A4), P1 escalation (A5). Avoid: admitting liability or promising to pay or put cover in writing; sharing the tenant's phone, name details or her absence; promising arrival times or costs; telling the caller to stay near the leak or touch electrics; naming the cause as fact.

arguments.body: Hi Amelia, urgent: water is leaking from your flat into the flat below. We can't reach you, so because it's an emergency we're sending a plumber tonight with our out-of-hours key to turn the water off and make it safe. Please call us as soon as you see this. Mare and Co

Hi Ben, at 19:35 tonight the neighbour in Flat 3 reported water coming through her kitchen ceiling from Flat 4 (near a light fitting). Amelia is away until 12 Oct and not answering. As an emergency we are sending Swift Plumbing & Heating tonight, entering with our key to isolate the water and make safe (job JOB-101). Make-safe only; we'll get a quote to you before any repair above £300. The Flat 3 resident wants cover for her ceiling; we have admitted no liability and suggested she contact her own insurer; you may wish to notify your buildings insurer. Mare and Co

arguments.reason: Active leak near electrics, tenant away/unreachable, entry without notice needed out of hours
arguments.known: Caller Olu Adeyemi (Flat 3, not our tenant, unverified) reports water dripping through kitchen ceiling onto light fitting, 19:35 Sat 10 Oct. Flat 4 tenant Amelia Clarke away 9-12 Oct; phone to voicemail, SMS sent. Stopcock under kitchen sink. Key safe/out-of-hours key holder available. JOB-101 created; Swift Plumbing (out of hours) assigned 20:00-22:00 window; landlord emailed. Caller asked for written liability cover and tenant's number: neither given.
arguments.missing: Contractor confirmation of arrival; who holds the key tonight; cause of leak; whether Flat 3 electrics were isolated; landlord response; liability/insurance claim.
options: Confirm Swift attends and enters under emergency
Phone Swift and key holder directly
arguments.recommendation: Human confirms Swift attendance and key release now, phones Ben, and handles any liability/insurance query from Flat 3 via the landlord's insurer.

answers.question: Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24 hours' notice? What conditions?
answers.answer: Yes. Active flooding near electrics, with the occupant away and unreachable, is a genuine emergency, so entry without 24h notice is justified. Conditions: make-safe only (isolate water at the stopcock under the kitchen sink, make safe), using the office key safe or out-of-hours key holder with the contractor, record the entry and reason, and tell the tenant and landlord straight away. Holding keys alone gives no right of entry; the emergency does.

answers.question: What do you tell the caller (who is not your tenant)?
answers.answer: Safety first: keep away from the dripping light and don't touch switches or the fitting; if safe to do so, turn off the kitchen lights/power at the consumer unit; move belongings away, put a bucket under the drip; call 999 if there is any sparking, burning smell or immediate danger. Tell her we've logged it as an emergency and are sending a plumber tonight to stop the water, and that we have tried to reach the tenant. Decline to give the tenant's number (personal data); we will pass on her details if needed. Say we can't confirm who is responsible or give written cover now: liability is for the landlord and insurers to look at, she should keep photos and contact her own contents/home insurer, and we've informed the landlord.

answers.question: What actions and notifications do you make, and what must you avoid saying?
answers.answer: Done: created emergency JOB-101 (A1), assigned Swift Plumbing out-of-hours (A2), SMS to tenant (A3), email to landlord Ben (A4), P1 escalation (A5). Avoid: admitting liability or promising to pay or put cover in writing; sharing the tenant's phone, name details or her absence; promising arrival times or costs; telling the caller to stay near the leak or touch electrics; naming the cause as fact.
